title: How the Paleo Diet Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the Paleo (Paleolithic) diet, which was popularized by Dr. Loren Cordain's 2002 book and modeled on pre-agricultural hunter-gatherer eating. They cover its emphasis on lean protein, low-glycemic carbs, fiber, and healthy fats, and its avoidance of grains, legumes, dairy, processed food, salt and refined sugar. The hosts discuss the controversy over the saturated fat and heart disease hypothesis (Ancel Keys' Six Countries and Seven Countries studies), LDL subfractions, the Maasai diet, and the low-fat trend linked to rising obesity and diabetes. They close with a US News ranking of 32 diets (Paleo ranked last), advice to be your own health advocate and read studies critically, and a listener mail defending B.F. Skinner's air crib and correcting an earlier remark about Subway bread.

segments.title: Opening banter and Squarespace read
segments.summary: Opening banter with Josh and Chuck, followed by a Squarespace sponsor read.

segments.title: Origins of the Paleo diet
segments.summary: Introduction of the Paleo diet by Dr. Loren Cordain's 2002 book, its motivation as a response to processed Western food, and the idea of eating like pre-agricultural hunter-gatherers. Walter Voegtlin's 1975 self-published book The Stone Age Diet is mentioned as an earlier version.

segments.title: Evidence debate and the limits of diet science
segments.summary: The hosts question the unsubstantiated claim that modern bodies match Paleolithic physiology, note that every diet has supporting and opposing studies, and argue that science does not yet have a settled baseline.

segments.title: Paleo food list: protein, carbs, and glycemic index
segments.summary: Describes Paleo emphasis on higher protein and lower, slow-burning carbohydrates, with glycemic index (about 55 or lower) explained, and notes that glycemic index values vary with ripeness.

segments.title: Fiber, net carbs, and fats
segments.summary: Discusses fiber as part of the diet, net carbohydrate counting used in low-carb diets, and the higher intake of omega-3 and omega-6 fats.

segments.title: Recap of Paleo foods and mid-episode break
segments.summary: Recap of foods included and excluded on the Paleo diet, followed by a break.

segments.title: Saturated fat and the Ancel Keys studies
segments.summary: Covers the saturated fat and heart disease hypothesis, Ancel Keys' Six Countries and Seven Countries studies, criticisms of cherry-picked data, and the meaning of 'saturated' in fatty acid chemistry.

segments.title: LDL subfractions and the Maasai
segments.summary: Discusses LDL particle subfractions, the reasonable view of Ronald Krauss at UC Berkeley, and the Maasai who eat a fat-heavy diet with low cholesterol, whose risk rose after moving to cities.

segments.title: Low-fat trend, obesity, and dairy
segments.summary: Explains how the low-fat push led to added sugar and salt in low-fat foods and rising obesity and diabetes rates. Discusses whole milk versus skim milk, fat-soluble vitamins, and Paleo's avoidance of dairy.

segments.title: Squarespace read
segments.summary: Repeat sponsor read for Squarespace with offer code.

segments.title: Paleo rules, studies, and the US News diet ranking
segments.summary: Discusses the Paleo rule allowing about three non-Paleo meals a week and the lack of definitive research. Reviews the US News ranking of 32 diets, with DASH first and Paleo last, and a 2009 small diabetes study cited in the article.

segments.title: Takeaways and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts advise being your own health advocate and reading study abstracts. They close with show contact information.

segments.title: Listener mail: defending B.F. Skinner
segments.summary: A listener named Hake defends B.F. Skinner's air crib as a climate-controlled crib, not a box, and the hosts correct an earlier Subway bread remark.
